title: 10. Get started with speech in Azure · Checkpoint
slo: Review the key concepts of 10. Get started with speech in Azure.

exercises.question_text: What can point batch transcription to audio files in storage?

options.rationale: A shared access signature, or SAS, URI can point batch transcription to stored audio files. It is used with audio in storage.

options.error_type: Confuses an audio-file URI with a recognition object
options.rationale: A SpeechRecognizer performs transcription in an application. It is not the URI that points batch work to stored audio.
options.better_fit: Use a SpeechRecognizer to perform transcription after configuring audio input.

feedback.intrinsic: The stored file location would still be missing.
feedback.instructional: A SAS URI identifies audio in storage for batch transcription.

options.error_type: Confuses storage access with service connection
options.rationale: An endpoint connects an application to Azure Speech. It does not point batch transcription to an audio file in storage.
options.better_fit: Use an endpoint when initializing a connection to Azure Speech.

feedback.intrinsic: The batch request would not identify the stored recording.
feedback.instructional: Connection details and a stored-file URI have different roles.

options.rationale: A speech key is used for authentication. It is not a pointer to stored audio.
options.better_fit: Use a speech key with an endpoint to authenticate a connection.

feedback.intrinsic: The audio file location would still not be supplied.
feedback.instructional: Authentication proves access; a SAS URI points to the stored audio.

exercises.explanation: Correct. A SAS URI can point batch transcription to audio files in storage.

exercises.question_text: Synthesized speech is used to convert customer calls into written transcripts.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This would treat a written-record task as though it produced spoken output.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Synthesized speech generates audio; speech recognition converts calls into written transcripts.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Customer-call transcripts use speech recognition.

exercises.question_text: Speech synthesis generates spoken output from text-based data.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This would incorrectly rule out the capability used to make written content audible.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Speech synthesis, also called text-to-speech, generates spoken output from text-based data.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Speech synthesis creates audible speech from text-based data.

exercises.question_text: A retailer needs spoken product updates in several languages and regional pronunciations. Which Azure Speech voice options can it choose for its Text-to-Speech API solution?

options.rationale: Predefined voices are available through the API. They support multiple languages and regional pronunciation.
Neural voices are available through the API. They use neural networks for more natural sounding speech.
Custom voices can be developed and used with the API. They are an available voice option.
Speech-to-text converts spoken audio into text. It is not a voice option for generating product updates.
options.better_fit: Use this when customer speech needs to become written text.

feedback.intrinsic: The retailer could transcribe speech but could not select a voice for product updates.
feedback.instructional: Text-to-speech voice options include predefined, neural, and custom voices.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Predefined, neural, and custom voices are available for Text-to-Speech.

exercises.question_text: Reconstruct the statement from the pieces.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The relationship between speech and feedback is unclear.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Place listening to learner speech before the feedback.

exercises.correct_answer: Learning apps listen to students speak then provide pronunciation feedback
exercises.explanation: Learning apps listen to learners speaking, then provide pronunciation feedback.

exercises.question_text: Azure Speech supports both prebuilt and custom Speech service models.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A team might wrongly assume every model must be built from scratch.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Azure Speech supports both prebuilt and custom models.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Azure Speech supports prebuilt and custom models for speech tasks.

exercises.question_text: A language-learning app designer wants to hear a practice sentence with a different synthetic voice and a new speed setting. Where should the designer test these changes?

options.rationale: This playground lets users choose a synthetic voice and adjust speed. It then generates audio from text.
The Speech-to-Text playground is for testing spoken input and transcription. It does not provide the requested voice and speed controls for generated speech.
options.better_fit: Use this when testing how recorded or microphone audio becomes written text.

feedback.intrinsic: The designer could test transcription but would not hear the sentence with the requested changes.
feedback.instructional: Use the Text-to-Speech playground to adjust voice and speed for generated audio.

options.rationale: Batch transcription processes stored audio into text. It does not generate speech from a practice sentence.
options.better_fit: Use this for stored recordings that need transcription results.

feedback.intrinsic: The practice sentence would not be spoken with a new voice or speed.
feedback.instructional: Batch transcription is audio-to-text work; synthetic voice controls belong in Text-to-Speech.

options.error_type: Confuses text-to-speech with recognition SDK objects
options.rationale: A SpeechRecognizer object recognizes spoken audio in application code. It does not generate spoken audio from written text.
options.better_fit: Use this when writing an application that recognizes microphone or audio-file speech.

feedback.intrinsic: The designer would be set up to listen for speech rather than hear the written sentence.
feedback.instructional: Use the Text-to-Speech playground for generated speech with adjustable delivery.

exercises.explanation: Correct. The Text-to-Speech Foundry playground supports synthetic voice and speed changes.

exercises.question_text: Batch transcription returns results ___.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The result timing would be described incorrectly.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Batch transcription returns results asynchronously; real-time transcription is used when text is needed during live speech.

exercises.explanation: Asynchronously means results arrive after the request is submitted rather than immediately. This timing supports batch processing of stored recordings.

exercises.question_text: The Speech-to-Text SDK is used only after a completed transcription and cannot send audio.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The app would have no way to provide its microphone, file, or stream audio for transcription.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The SDK can capture or send audio securely to Azure Speech, then return transcription in near real time or after processing.

exercises.explanation: Correct! The SDK can capture or send audio before transcription results are returned.

exercises.question_text: A customer-support lead needs callers' spoken words turned into text for staff review. Which results show the app is using speech recognition? Select all that apply.

options.text: The call becomes a text transcript
options.rationale: A transcript is spoken audio converted into text. This is a direct recognition result.
Detecting spoken input is part of speech recognition. It happens before transcription.

options.text: The app interprets the caller's speech
options.rationale: Recognition interprets spoken input to produce usable data. It does more than store raw audio.

options.text: The app reads a typed reply aloud
options.rationale: Reading typed text aloud is text-to-speech. It does not show that speech became text.
options.better_fit: This fits a support bot that gives spoken responses from text.

feedback.intrinsic: Staff would not receive the requested transcript.
feedback.instructional: Review requires speech to be converted into usable text.

exercises.explanation: Correct. These outcomes show spoken input becoming usable text.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the following steps in speech synthesis.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Putting audio before earlier stages breaks the path from text to spoken output.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Follow the synthesis sequence from text, to sounds, to phonemes, to audio.

exercises.correct_answer: Tokenize the text Assign phonetic sounds Create phonemes Synthesize audio
exercises.explanation: Speech synthesis starts with text, assigns phonetic sounds, creates phonemes, and then synthesizes audio.

exercises.question_text: After phonemes are mapped to words, the result is recognized ___.

parts.text: After phonemes are mapped to words, the result is recognized

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The answer would name an earlier representation or the wrong output.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The phoneme-to-word stage produces recognized text.

exercises.explanation: A language model maps phonemes to words, producing recognized text.

exercises.question_text: A retail manager wants a shopping assistant that understands spoken order-status questions and says answers aloud. Which capability should the team use?

options.rationale: The assistant needs spoken input and spoken output. AI speech capabilities cover both voice needs.
Speech recognition can understand the spoken question. It does not by itself create a spoken answer.
options.better_fit: This fits a task that only transcribes spoken customer requests.

feedback.intrinsic: Customers could ask aloud but would not hear a reply.
feedback.instructional: The scenario requires both recognition and spoken output.

options.rationale: Speech synthesis can speak an answer aloud. It cannot interpret a spoken question by itself.
options.better_fit: This fits reading already-written order updates aloud.

feedback.intrinsic: The assistant could speak but not understand the question.

options.rationale: A text-only interface does not meet the voice requirement. The scenario calls for speaking and hearing.
options.better_fit: This fits a shopping page where users type and read.

feedback.intrinsic: Customers would need to type and read.
feedback.instructional: Choose AI speech for two-way voice interaction.

exercises.explanation: Correct. The assistant needs spoken input and spoken output.

exercises.question_text: ___ handles live incoming speech.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The live speaker would not receive text as the speech happens.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Batch transcription is for stored recordings; use real-time transcription for incoming audio.

exercises.explanation: Incoming audio must be handled while it is being spoken. That timing distinguishes real-time transcription from processing recordings later.

exercises.question_text: Put the object relationship in order.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The distinct roles of the two objects are reversed or obscured.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: First identify what creates audio, then identify what chooses its destination.

exercises.correct_answer: SpeechSynthesizer creates synthesized audio AudioOutputConfig chooses its destination
exercises.explanation: SpeechSynthesizer creates audio, and AudioOutputConfig determines its destination.

exercises.question_text: A media platform is setting up live captioning, but its new transcription app cannot connect to Azure Speech. Which setup information should the developer provide? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: The endpoint is the service address required to connect to the Azure resource. The SDK initialization uses this address.
A resource key authenticates a connection made to the endpoint. It is one supported authentication method.
Microsoft Entra ID is an identity-based authentication alternative to a resource key. It can be used for SDK initialization.

options.error_type: Confuses setup credentials with a result notification
options.rationale: A recognized event returns completed text after recognition. It cannot provide the endpoint or authenticate a connection.
options.better_fit: Choose this when handling completed transcription during recognition.

feedback.intrinsic: The app would still lack the information needed to connect.
feedback.instructional: For connection setup, provide the endpoint and one authentication method. A recognized event is a result notification, not setup information.

exercises.explanation: Correct! The app needs the endpoint plus authentication; a resource key and Microsoft Entra ID are supported authentication choices.

exercises.question_text: A media team submits archived show recordings for batch transcription. Which expectations should the producer set? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: A batch job normally starts within minutes after submission. This is a common expectation, not a guarantee.
Batch jobs are scheduled on a best-effort basis. The exact transition to running is not guaranteed.

options.text: Its running time is not guaranteed
options.rationale: There is no guaranteed time for a batch job to change to running. The producer should not promise an exact time.

options.text: It will transcribe while performers speak
options.error_type: Confuses batch work with real-time transcription
options.rationale: Archived shows are stored recordings. Transcription while people speak is a real-time use case.
options.better_fit: Use real-time transcription for a live performance that needs text while it happens.

feedback.intrinsic: The producer could promise captions during an event that has already been recorded.
feedback.instructional: Archived recordings fit batch processing, not live incoming transcription.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Archived recordings fit batch transcription, whose scheduling is best-effort and not guaranteed.

exercises.question_text: Reconstruct the statement from the pieces.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The sentence no longer clearly connects stored audio with later results.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Place the method first, then its input, followed by the timing of its result.

exercises.correct_answer: Batch transcription processes stored recordings and returns results later
exercises.explanation: The sentence names the method, identifies stored recordings as its input, and states that results arrive later. Those details define batch transcription.

exercises.question_text: A retail virtual-assistant app must listen to a customer's spoken request until the customer ends the conversation. Which action should the developer use?

options.rationale: Continuous recognition keeps listening until the application stops it. This fits a spoken conversation that continues until the customer finishes.

options.error_type: Confuses receiving completed text with keeping audio listening
options.rationale: A recognized event provides completed text. It does not start or keep recognition listening.
options.better_fit: Choose this when the app needs to handle a completed transcription result.

feedback.intrinsic: The app could receive a result but would not begin ongoing listening.
feedback.instructional: Use continuous recognition to keep listening. Handle a recognized event when completed text arrives.

options.error_type: Confuses choosing an input source with starting recognition
options.rationale: AudioConfig specifies the microphone or other audio source. It does not begin speech recognition.
options.better_fit: Choose this when setting the audio input source before creating the recognizer.

feedback.intrinsic: The microphone could be selected, but listening would not start.
feedback.instructional: AudioConfig identifies where audio comes from. Start continuous recognition to begin and continue listening.

options.error_type: Confuses connection setup with starting recognition
options.rationale: SpeechConfig supplies endpoint and authentication information. It does not start recognition of the customer's speech.
options.better_fit: Choose this when supplying the Azure Speech connection details.

feedback.intrinsic: The connection could be configured, but the conversation would not yet be listened to.
feedback.instructional: SpeechConfig prepares the connection. Start continuous recognition when the app is ready to listen.

exercises.explanation: Correct! Continuous recognition keeps listening until the application stops it.

exercises.question_text: A retailer must generate thousands of announcements overnight for stores to play the next day. Which decisions best fit this situation? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: A backend can process announcements without immediate user playback. It fits overnight generation for later use.

options.text: Generate audio files for later playback
options.rationale: The stores need reusable audio the next day. Saved files support delayed playback.

options.text: Use a client app for immediate playback
options.rationale: Client apps suit speech that must play immediately. This requirement is batch preparation for later playback.
options.better_fit: Use this when a user needs to hear speech immediately in an app.

feedback.intrinsic: The announcements would not be prepared as next-day files.
feedback.instructional: Match later use with a backend that generates audio files.

options.text: Use AudioOutputConfig as the main service
options.rationale: AudioOutputConfig controls an audio destination. It does not decide the client-versus-backend architecture.
options.better_fit: Use this when selecting where synthesized audio is delivered.

feedback.intrinsic: The overnight generation plan would still be missing.
feedback.instructional: Choose the backend architecture first; configure output separately.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Backend-generated files fit overnight preparation and next-day playback.

exercises.question_text: A set of rules and endpoints that lets one application use another service is an ___.

parts.text: A set of rules and endpoints that lets one application use another service is an

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The communication role would remain unclear.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Choose API for the rules and endpoints. An endpoint is an address, a resource key is a credential, and the SDK is client-library code.

exercises.explanation: An API defines how one application can access another application's functions or data. An endpoint is part of an API, while a key authenticates access and an SDK provides ready-made code.

exercises.question_text: The Azure Text-to-Speech SDK can generate natural-sounding audio using ___.

parts.text: The Azure Text-to-Speech SDK can generate natural-sounding audio using

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The intended voice technology would not be identified.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Neural voices generate spoken audio from written text.

exercises.explanation: Neural voices produce the synthesized spoken output.

exercises.question_text: Order the pieces correctly.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The sentence would not clearly connect the library to transcription.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Name the SDK first, identify it as a client library, and then describe its audio-to-text purpose.

exercises.correct_answer: The Speech-to-Text SDK is a client library that converts spoken audio into written text
exercises.explanation: The first part names the component, then identifies its type, then states the conversion it supports. This connects the SDK's client-library role to transcription.

exercises.question_text: In a text-to-speech flow, the app receives text results after Azure Speech analyzes microphone audio.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Written input would be handled as microphone audio.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: TTS sends text and receives generated audio.

exercises.explanation: Correct. That describes speech-to-text.
